details.title: Arban – Ornament Study No. 45
details.lead: From Arban's Grande méthode complète de cornet à pistons et de saxhorn, first edition, 1864. The notes are the cornet part as printed, in written pitch for the B♭ cornet. Below: the book's own words, translated from the French.
facts: Arban, Grande méthode complète de cornet à pistons et de saxhorn, first edition (Paris: Léon Escudier, 1864)

The appoggiaturas are written out as the book prints them, the way they are played: the accented note on the beat, then the note it leans into. The small notes are graces played quickly before their note.

sections.heading: The simple appoggiatura
paragraphs: The simple appoggiatura is a small note that is no part of the chord, and that nevertheless takes half the length of the note before which it stands (Example 8).
The appoggiatura can be placed above or below any note. When it is above, it can be a whole step or a half step away; when it is below, it must always be a half step away (Example 9).

In the music of the old masters there are a great many appoggiaturas that must take half the length of the note they come before; but today, so that everyone plays them alike, music is generally written as it is to be played, which is beyond question much better. (See Nos. 44 to 47.)

sections.heading: A word on all of these
paragraphs: Since all the lessons on ornaments were written to serve as studies, I have brought together, on purpose and in abundance, every kind of ornament. But take great care not to overuse them so in practice, for that would be in the worst of taste.

sources.title: IMSLP: Grande méthode complète de cornet à pistons (Arban), first edition, Paris 1864
